entities.summary:
Isfrid of Ratzeburg was a Premonstratensian Prince-Bishop of Ratzeburg, a prominent figure in the medieval period of Germany. As the Prince-Bishop of Ratzeburg, Isfrid played a crucial role in the governance and administration of the region, which was a significant center of power and influence in the Holy Roman Empire.

Born in unknown, Isfrid rose to prominence through his connections to the Holy Roman Emperor and his role in the politics of the region. His tenure as Prince-Bishop of Ratzeburg lasted from 1198 to 1204, during which time he oversaw various religious, cultural, and economic developments in the region.

Isfrid's legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Premonstratensian order in the region, as well as his contributions to the development of the region's architecture, art, and education. His impact on the region's history can be felt through the many churches, monasteries, and other institutions he established or supported.

Isfrid of Ratzeburg died on June 22, 1204, leaving behind a lasting legacy in the region. His life and work serve as a testament to the enduring power of the Catholic Church in the medieval period.
